description: NASA Space Apps Challenge için bilim, teknoloji ve uzay alanlarında yenilikçi fikirler geliştirebileceğimiz bir ekip kuruyorum. Takım çalışmasına, yaratıcılığa ve birlikte öğrenmeye önem veriyorum. Yazılım, yapay zeka, veri analizi, web geliştirme, astronomi, tasarım ve problem çözme alanlarına ilgi duyan ekip arkadaşları arıyorum. Deneyimden çok öğrenme isteğine, sorumluluk bilincine ve üretkenliğe değer veriyorum.
summary:
NASAlytics is a health monitoring tool that lets astronauts assess their own health and act on it when Earth is minutes away or out of contact. One screen shows a clickable 3D body, ten health indicators with color, icon and text status, step-by-step guidance, a daily routine with gamification and a voice assistant that speaks Turkish and English. A crew medical officer view shows the whole crew live, and a ground view shows the same data late by the real communication delay of the chosen environment, from the ISS to Mars.

The core is deliberately not AI. Alarms come from a deterministic rule engine built on NASA-STD-3001 and clinical thresholds, and intervention cards are taken verbatim from NASA medical checklists. The language model only summarizes and ranks; it cannot write a dose. Every number on screen is tagged with its origin, so real NASA measurements (ISS and Mars radiation, Inspiration4 lab panels, live DONKI space weather) are never confused with simulated vitals.

It matters because on a Mars mission an answer from Earth can take 44 minutes. The crew needs something they can trust on their own.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

NASAlytics gathers health indicators (blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep, mood, SpO2, respiration, cabin CO2 and more) by live stream, manual entry, voice and camera, evaluates them, and tells the astronaut what to do and who to involve: yourself, the crew medical officer, or the flight surgeon on the ground.

HOW IT WORKS

Three layers. (1) A deterministic rule engine in the browser raises alarms from thresholds in NASA-STD-3001 and AHA/ADA/CDC guidelines; it works with no internet. (2) A library of intervention cards copied from the ISS emergency medical procedures and the NASA JSC-48031 medical checklist, with drug, dose and page as printed. (3) A language model that summarizes the situation and ranks the cards. It can reference a drug only by library ID, and any dose it writes is stripped on the server.

Three connected views run over WebSockets: astronaut, crew medical officer (live), and ground control (delayed by the real one-way light time of the selected environment). A loss-of-signal mode holds data on board and delivers it when the link returns; cloud AI goes quiet while rules and cards keep working.

OTHER FEATURES

Clickable 3D body with organ, skeleton and muscle layers and NASA explanations per organ; tap-to-report symptoms; automatic crew alert if a critical alarm is not acknowledged; a crew medical record with BMI and an allergy check that blocks matching drugs; NASA exercise countermeasures with a personal heart-rate target; daily routine with streaks and badges; an on-device fatigue camera; ten scenarios including replays of the September 2017 (ISS) and May 2024 (Mars) solar storms from measured data; six mission environments; Turkish and English; works on phones.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Medical autonomy for Moon and Mars crews, where an answer from Earth can take up to 44 minutes. The same approach applies on Earth wherever a doctor is far away: Antarctic stations, submarines, ships, rural clinics.

WHAT IS CREATIVE ABOUT IT

The safety design: AI is useful but is not allowed to decide or to dose. Every number shows its provenance (NASA measurement, NASA standard, clinical guideline, projection, assumption, simulated). Real storms are replayed instead of invented ones. The ground view makes communication delay something you can see.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Scientific validity above all: we show nothing as real that is not. Vital signs are simulated and labelled. We did not invent exercise loads or risk judgements that NASA does not publish, and our own assumptions are labelled as assumptions. Accessibility: status is never color alone. Privacy: camera frames stay on the device. Security: API keys stay on the server behind rate limits, request size limits, origin checks and a daily spending cap.

TOOLS

React 19, TypeScript, three.js, zustand, Vite; Python FastAPI, WebSockets; MediaPipe; Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5; Gemini text-to-speech; Playwright for testing; hosted on our own server.
